reader.requirement: The implementor specifies the subset of RANDOM's argument-1 domain that yields distinct pseudo-random sequences, and that subset includes every seed 0 through 32767.

SAME-SEED-SAME (literal 32767 vs COMP expression SB + 1), 32766-VS-32767-DISTINCT, 32768-DISTINCT, SEED0-RESTARTS, BIGSEED-IN-RANGE (seed 999999999999999999)

reader.notes: The subset is specified in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-145.md: every seed 0..2^31-1 selects its own System.Random state (seed AND 0x7FFFFFFF), measured distinct over 0..65535 by unit test. The probe confirmed at --std 85 that all 32768 required seeds give distinct sequences.

refuter.evidence: §1989:A.2.35.4 RV3 asks only that the implementor specify the subset and that it include 0..32767; DOC-A.1-145 specifies 0..2^31-1 and the reader measured all 32768 required seeds distinct. rrand.cob at 85 (runs/rrand-001), aimed at the documented subset's edge: seed 0 and seed 2147483647 give the SAME first, second and fourth draws (0.72624326996795980, 0.81732535959096870, 0.55816119143653720) and differ only in the 9th digit of the third (0.76802268939466340 vs 0.76802269218863120): distinct sequences, so the documented subset holds literally, though the two are near-aliases (System.Random's Knuth seeding reduces MSEED - seed modulo 2^31-1, and 0 and 2^31-1 are congruent). Not a breach of RV3 (outside the required floor and still distinct); worth a note on DOC-A.1-145. Refusals at 85: RANDOM(1.5) COBOL1627, RANDOM(AN) COBOL1627. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.35.4 RV3 the text is in RV3.
